transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. We're at the pre-load review, so let's get current before I issue the binding manifest. We have three cargoes — a 3,800-kg engineering pallet, a 1,200-kg refrigerated medical-supply crate, and 1,800 kg of general stores — and three vehicles: V-1 and V-2 rated at 5,000 kg each, and V-3 rated at 3,000 kg. Each cargo rides on a single vehicle and no vehicle carries more than one cargo. Logistics and motor-pool reps, please report any current cargo or vehicle constraints I should know about before I finalize the loading plan.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Captain, I have a constraint to report. The refrigerated medical-supply crate is approved only for V-3 because its temperature-control unit requires V-3's installed inverter. I confirmed the compatibility label with the medical supply section this morning, but the manifest worksheet still lists the vehicle as unassigned.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Captain, I need to report a vehicle constraint. V-2 has a temporary 3,000-kilogram payload limit until its rear-suspension inspection is completed. I recorded the restriction in the motor-pool inspection log this morning, but the fleet status board hasn't been updated yet, so it still shows V-2 at its normal 5,000-kilogram rating. This means the 3,800-kilogram engineering pallet cannot go on V-2.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Captain, to summarize the motor-pool side: V-2 is limited to 3,000 kg right now, so it can only safely take the 1,200-kg medical crate or the 1,800-kg general stores. The 3,800-kg engineering pallet needs to go on V-1, since V-1 is still rated at 5,000 kg. Once Sgt. Patel's constraint is factored in, the medical crate is approved only for V-3, so that leaves V-2 for the 1,800-kg general stores. I'll also make sure the fleet status board gets updated today so we don't have this gap at the next review.
